title: Key Management Operational Playbook (KMS/HSM/BYOK)
content:
Purpose:
This operational playbook defines runbook-level procedures and automation patterns for Key Management at Redwood Inference. It covers KMS and HSM usage, BYOK onboarding and proofs, rotation procedures (regular and emergency), encryption-at-rest architecture decisions, RBAC v2 mappings for key access, and SIEM/export formats for audit evidence used in compliance assessments.

Scope and intended audience:
- Scope: All customer and platform encryption keys used to protect data-at-rest (DEKs, KEKs, wrapping keys, tenant keys), key stores (managed KMS, HSM appliances, customer BYOK material), and processes that generate cryptographic evidence for auditors.
- Audience: security-engineering, platform-ops, SRE, product-engineering responsible for private and hosted deployments, compliance reviewers.

High-level design decisions (summary):
- Envelope encryption is mandatory for all persisted customer data. Platform stores only encrypted data keys (DEKs). The master/wrapping keys (KEKs) live in HSM-backed KMS or customer BYOK HSMs.
- We support three KEK deployment modes: Redwood-managed cloud KMS (default), Dedicated HSM cluster for Dedicated customers, and customer-provided BYOK (import or external HSM via PKCS#11 / KMIP gateway).
- All KEKs are configured with key usage policies: only Unwrap/Decrypt for runtime services and Wrap/Encrypt for rotation services. Private key material never leaves HSM boundary.

RBAC v2 mapping (KMS-related roles):
- security:kms-admin -> full key lifecycle (create, schedule-rotation, disable, destroy) reserved for SecOps and Security-Engineering owners.
- infra:kms-operator -> can create DEKs, request encryption/decryption operations, and read key metadata; cannot export key material. Assigned to platform services and SRE.
- product:tenant-key-owner -> limited to creating tenant DEKs and attaching metadata; cannot access KEKs or raw key material.
- audit:read-only -> view key metadata, usage logs, and rotation history.
Implementation notes: RBAC v2 policy engine enforces attribute-based constraints (environment, region, customer-tier) at request-time; map KMS policy statements to RBAC v2 groups and include conditional checks for private deployments.

Audit log schema (KMS/HSM events) - canonical event fields (SIEM-friendly):
- event_id: UUID
- timestamp: ISO8601
- principal: user/service account (RBAC v2 ID)
- principal_role: top-level role mapping (e.g., infra:kms-operator)
- action: (KeyCreate|KeyRotateInitiate|KeyRotateComplete|KeyEncrypt|KeyDecrypt|KeyImport|KeyDisable|KeyScheduleDestroy|KeyDestroy|KeyPolicyChange)
- key_id: opaque identifier (kept stable across rotations)
- key_alias: human-friendly alias (tenant-123/db-accounts-dek)
- key_type: (KEK|DEK|WRAPPING_KEY)
- key_origin: (RedwoodKMS|HSM|BYOK-Imported|BYOK-External)
- algorithm: e.g., AES-256-GCM, RSA-3072
- operation_result: (Success|Failure|Denied)
- error_code: string (if failure)
- request_context: small JSON-stringified map (caller_ip, region, request_id)
- correlation_id: upstream request id for traceability

SIEM export format and retention:
- Exports: events are streamed in near-real-time to Splunk/Chronicle via an encrypted delivery stream. We push newline-delimited JSON. Field names use snake_case to match enterprise SIEM parsers.
- Retention: raw KMS event logs retained for 2 years in cold storage; indexed SIEM searchable for 1 year by default. Retention exceptions can be configured per-customer for Dedicated/Private contracts.
- Example NDJSON line:
{
  "event_id": "b6106a6f-2d2a-4a6e-b4c1-0f12e3b9c9a2",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-18T15:12:33Z",
  "principal": "svc-platform-encryptor@redwood",
  "principal_role": "infra:kms-operator",
  "action": "KeyDecrypt",
  "key_id": "k-0a9f3c",
  "key_alias": "tenant-42-main-dek",
  "key_type": "DEK",
  "key_origin": "RedwoodKMS",
  "algorithm": "AES-256-GCM",
  "operation_result": "Success",
  "request_context": "{\"caller_ip\": \"10.23.55.4\", \"region\": \"us-west-2\", \"request_id\": \"req-9f2a\"}",
  "correlation_id": "req-9f2a"
}

Evidence automation patterns (for audits):
- Triggered snapshots: weekly snapshot job gathers key metadata, policy versions, active rotations, and the last 12 months of related audit events for a given target key set. Snapshots are signed with an internal signing key and archived in the compliance bucket.
- Replayable evidence bundle: For each compliance request we produce a bundle containing: key inventory CSV, rotation timeline (timestamps and operators), NDJSON audit stream slice, RBAC v2 membership export, and signed proof artifacts (HSM attestation when available). Bundles are generated by an automation runner (serverless function) and uploaded to a retention-controlled artifact store.
- Minimal manual steps: automation provides a prefilled review checklist; an approver (security reviewer) must confirm non-technical items before bundle is sealed.

Key rotation procedures (routine):
1) Pre-checks: verify backups of encrypted DEKs, current rotation window, and policy approvals. 2) Schedule a quiet window (if required) and notify stakeholders (SRE, product owner, any customer contacts for Dedicated/BYO-K). 3) Generate new KEK (or request wrap-only key in BYOK external HSM). 4) Rewrap active DEKs: use streaming rewrap job that reads ciphertext, unwraps with old KEK inside HSM boundary, rewraps with new KEK; ensures atomic write via idempotent write tokens. 5) Validate: run sample decrypt tests across regions and tenant set, check metrics for error spikes. 6) Complete rotation: update key aliases/metadata, set old KEK to Disabled (retained for emergency rollback for retention window), record rotation event in audit log. 7) Finalize: after retention window and successful monitoring, schedule old KEK for destruction.

Notes for BYOK and external HSMs:
- BYOK import vs external: Imported BYOK (customer uploads key material) behaves like Redwood-managed key with restrictions (no plaintext export). External BYOK (customer keeps key on-prem/HSM) is accessed via remote KMIP/PKCS#11 bridge; rewrap operations must be negotiated (some external HSMs disallow key usage for bulk rewrap). Document constraints in onboarding checklist.
- Attestations: collect HSM manufacturer attestation (e.g., FIPS 140-2/3 module cert) and a signed key origin statement from the customer.

Emergency compromise recovery (high-level runbook):
- Detection: automated anomaly: rapid successive key_decrypt failures, unknown principal usage, or SIEM alert.
- Rapid actions: 1) Set KEK to Disabled (immediate deny), 2) Rotate KEKs for affected dataset scope (create replacement key), 3) Initiate forensic capture (preserve logs, capture snapshots, lock down access), 4) Notify Legal/CS and affected customers per policy.
- Evidence: create a sealed incident bundle (same format as evidence bundle + incident timeline, related Jira ticket, Slack thread dump).

Testing and validation checklist (ops):
- Unit tests for key wrap/unwrap flows.
- End-to-end staging rewrap run across sample tenants.
- Failure injection: simulate KMS latency, HSM errors, and RBAC denial to validate graceful degradation and fallback policy.
- SIEM ingestion test: synthetic NDJSON events and full pipeline verification.
- Audit run: produce an evidence bundle and validate completeness against a standard checklist (rotations, policies, RBAC membership).

Operational automation snippets (references):
- Rewrap job pattern: streaming worker with checkpointed S3 processing, in-HSM unwrap/rewrap RPCs, idempotent writer with sequence tokens.
- Evidence runner: serverless orchestration (step function) that collects inventories, signs bundles, and pushes to compliance artifact store.
- SIEM forwarder: small daemon that batches KMS events and pushes NDJSON to the aggregator; includes retry and backpressure handling.

Appendices and references:
- Onboarding checklist for BYOK customers (keys to provide, attestation docs, network requirements).
- RBAC v2 policy templates for KMS roles (example policies and group assignments).
- Sample SIEM parsers (Splunk props/transforms snippet).
- Linked artifacts: Confluence KMS reference, linked Jira tickets, and implementation PRs (see linked_artifacts).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Confirm acceptable retention window for Dedicated enterprise customers > 2y (billing/contract implications).
- Standardize HSM attestation format we request during BYOK onboarding.
- Finalize mapping between RBAC v2 conditional policies and cloud KMS IAM rules to avoid drift.

Owner and maintenance:
- Document owner: Aisha Patel (security-eng).
- Quarterly review cadence and post-incident update requirement.
- Implementation owners: Security-Engineering for KMS features, Platform-Engineering for rewrap jobs, SRE for monitoring and SIEM integration.

This playbook is intentionally operationally prescriptive — it should be used by runbook automation, SRE rotations, and compliance artifact generation. For high-level architecture rationale and threats model see the KMS architecture spec (linked).
